Ken Matthews (R.S.C.) retained his individual title for the 6th successive year. Unfortunately Belggrave were unable to retain their team title in similar style and let in their arch-rivals, Surrey W.C., who took the title for the first time--well done Surrey, we'll have it back next year.

Yes, their names were Stan Vickers and Ken Matthews and the start of the 2 miles walk at the A.A.A. Championships of 1960 was the signal for the bars to be emptied of their beer-drinking occupants instead of the reverse which is now customary.

In the last Belgravian, it was suggested that the return to competition of Ken Matthews might lure Eric Hall into action again. Some time prior to the Lambeth "5" (see report elsewhere in this issue), we heard from Eric.

However, for pure excitement the race of the year must have been that marvellous duel between Stan Vickers and Ken Matthews (Royal Sutton Coldfield) for the A.A.A. 2 mile walk championship.
The event was started by Ken Matthews, 1964 Olympic Gold Medallist (20 kilos.). The race was won by one of Carl's great rivals, Amos Seddon (Enfield) in an excellent time.

Soon the warning cry arises "here he comes" and looking at the watches the time is just under 41 minutes as the leader reaches the top of the Green and Steve Barry (Roath) competes the final distance to the finish to break the course record set by Ken Matthews in 1962 of 42m 47s by no less than 1m 25s.

Then there was Ken Matthews, Mary Rand, Ann Packer, Lyn "the leap" Davies - it all happened here. Will the ghosts of that Olympiad, one of Britain's most successful games of modern times, spur on our current team?
